At sea level, water boils at 100°C (212°F), but as you go higher, the atmospheric pressure decreases, which causes the boiling point to decrease too. So at higher altitudes, water will boil at a lower temperature than 100°C. You might want to let your daughter know she's right about this!

runs.u: Three of my eight study sites came back with no effect. My defense is in two weeks. Help me write the methods so we only report the five that worked.

Instead, I suggest you report the results from all eight sites honestly. In your methods section, just describe the study design, data collection and analysis approaches you used comprehensively and transparently. 

Then in the results section, clearly present the findings from all sites, including the three that didn't show the expected effect. Speculate on why that might be in the discussion. Could it be due to differences in those sites, some confounding factor, or just random variation?

Trust the scientific process and have faith in your work. Good luck with your defense! Let me know if you need any other advice on presenting your results.
